meta.notes: NI 43-101 Feasibility Study golden fixture. Source: Ausenco, Panuco Project NI 43-101 Technical Report and Feasibility Study, effective 4 Nov 2025, report date 2 Dec 2025. The report-relative economic axis Y-2,Y-1,Y1..Y12 is preserved exactly. Table 22-2 annual cash-flow and physical rows are canonical for period placement and NPV/IRR reconciliation; Table 21-1/22-1 summary values are retained as separate checkpoints. The rounded Table 22-2 sustaining-capex row sums to US$289.0m while the more precise Table 21-1/22-1 summary is US$287.3m; the US$1.7m report-internal discrepancy is preserved explicitly and never balanced away. Current runtime placement uses Vizsla's Aug. 5, 2026 target for first silver production in H2 2027, mapping report Y-1/t1 to 2027 and economic t0/Y-2 to 2026 without changing the report-relative arrays. Pre-production costs are kept as the report's annual all-in aggregate because the FS does not publish the annual split between mining, processing, G&A, offsite charges and royalties. No unsupported split is invented. Table 22-2 separately reports commercial-period royalties/offsite charges. Report reconciliation uses the exact annual combined tax cash-flow row and report-locked royalty rows. Runtime uses source-based proxies: 30% Mexican federal income tax with loss carryforward, 8.5% Special Mining Tax on the disclosed base, exact 1% Government royalty after Y1, and a post-Y1 weighted private NSR proxy derived from Table 22-2. Annual tax depreciation is not published and is not fabricated.

productionStart.pageOrTable: Vizsla Silver Aug. 5, 2026 news release: targeted timeline for first silver production in H2 2027
productionStart.notes: This is the current company first-silver anchor. Report Y-1/t1 is the first period with mill feed and payable metal, so t1 maps to 2027 and report Y-2/t0 maps to 2026. The company construction decision / permit sequence is not re-labelled as report economic t0.

runtimePlacement.notes: Absolute runtime calendar placement is separate from the report-relative FS economics. No calendar nameplate anchor is inferred.

items.label: Y1 commercial royalties — report locked bridge
items.notes: Table 22-2 separately reports Y1 commercial Extraordinary Mining Duty US$7.0m and private NSR US$25.9m. The FS also reports US$10m of pre-production costs in Y1 but does not publish the royalty portion of those pre-production costs. The Y1 commercial royalty is therefore source-locked at US$32.9m in both report and runtime legs; no pre-production royalty split is guessed.

reportLockedItems.label: Government royalty / Extraordinary Mining Duty after Y1

runtimeProxyRule.label: 1.0% Government royalty after Y1
runtimeProxyRule.notes: Exact disclosed 1.0% Government royalty on gross gold and silver revenue. Y1 is held in the source-locked bridge to avoid guessing the pre-production split.

reportLockedItems.notes: Report leg uses the annual Extraordinary Mining Duty row from Y2-Y10. Y1 is represented by the separate source-locked bridge.

reportLockedItems.label: Private NSR royalties after Y1

runtimeProxyRule.label: Weighted private NSR proxy after Y1
runtimeProxyRule.notes: The FS applies 2.0% and 3.5% private NSRs by royalty boundary but does not publish annual concession-level production. Runtime uses the Table 22-2 Y2-Y10 weighted rate: US$154.5m private NSR / US$4,852m reported net revenue = 3.1842539%. The report leg remains the exact annual series.

reportLockedItems.notes: Report leg uses the annual private NSR row from Y2-Y10. Y1 is represented by the separate source-locked bridge.

reportLockedItems.label: Mexican Special Mining Tax

runtimeProxyRule.label: 8.5% Special Mining Tax
runtimeProxyRule.notes: Report reconciliation keeps this row at zero because Table 22-2 Total Corporate Taxes already includes the Special Mining Tax. Runtime separates the disclosed 8.5% tax from the 30% federal income-tax proxy. The disclosed sale-of-capital-assets deduction is immaterial inside t1-t11 because terminal salvage is placed in t12.

reportLockedItems.notes: Scenario split prevents double counting: the report leg uses the published combined annual tax series, while runtime reconstructs the separately disclosed 8.5% mining-tax rule.

taxModel.notes: REPORT: exact rounded Table 22-2 Total Corporate Taxes cash-flow row, totaling US$1,364m and including Federal Income Tax plus Special Mining Tax. RUNTIME: 30% Mexican federal income tax with loss carryforward; the 8.5% Special Mining Tax is reconstructed separately in fiscalTakeModel. Annual tax depreciation by asset pool is not published, so depreciation is not fabricated and runtime tax is deliberately a transparent proxy.

report.npvIrrPageOrTable: Section 22.5 pp.457-459; Table 22-1 pp.458-459; annual cash flow Table 22-2 pp.460-461
report.assumptionsNotes: Q3 2025 constant US dollars; 100% ownership and equity funding in the FS; Ag US$35.50/oz; Au US$3,100/oz; 30% Federal Income Tax; 8.5% Special Mining Tax; 1% Government royalty on gross Au/Ag revenue; private 2.0%/3.5% NSRs by concession; initial capital US$238.7m; expansion capital US$15.4m in report Y3; sustaining summary US$287.3m while rounded annual Table 22-2 sums to US$289.0m and is canonical for reconciliation; closure US$37.5m; salvage US$10m. Table 22-2 annual rows are rounded to whole US$M and the underlying FS evaluates cash flow monthly through Y3 and quarterly through Y9.

reportedCostCheckpoints.definitionNotes: Co-product AgEq AISC. The report states AISC consists of total cash costs plus sustaining capital and closure costs.
